extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS (Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech) is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It provides natural human speech and high quality transcripts for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation, and Retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages (including Afrikaans, Amharic, Arabic, Armenian, Assamese, Asturian, Azerbaijani, Belarusian, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Burmese, Cantonese Chinese, Catalan, Cebuano, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Filipino (Tagalog), Finnish, French, Fula, Galician, Ganda, Georgian, German, Greek, Gujarati, Hausa, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Igbo, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kabuverdianu, Kamba, Kannada, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Lao, Latvian, Lingala, Lithuanian, Luo, Luxembourgish, Macedonian, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Mandarin Chinese, Maori, Marathi, Mongolian, Nepali, Northern Sotho, Norwegian, Nyanja, Occitan, Oriya, Oromo, Pashto, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Shona, Sindhi, Slovak, Slovenian, Somali, Sorani Kurdish, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tajik, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Umbundu, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese, Welsh, Wolof, Xhosa, Yoruba, Zulu)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Starting with 2009 sentences from the dev and devtest sets of the FLoRes-101 dataset (split into train, dev, and test splits with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively), three recordings by three different native speakers were collected for each sentence in 102 languages, imposing a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponded to the input sentence, discarding invalid recordings.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 dev and devtest sentences, which originate from English Wikipedia and were translated into 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Recordings are kept as-is, from quiet or noisy environments, without data augmentations (e.g., SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation) with a speech sampling rate of 16kHz and segments within 30 seconds. For text transcripts, NFC and FST normalization are applied to each sentence, along with lower-casing, punctuation normalization and removal, splitting words into characters, and defining a token boundary. Three transcript versions are provided: original raw (SRC_RAW), preprocessed (SRC_NORM), and character-based (SRC_CHAR).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Recordings are evaluated by additional workers who assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Recordings were validated by human workers; if a recording did not match the input sentence it was discarded as invalid.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings were initially collected per sentence by three different native speakers, resulting in between zero and three validated recordings per sentence after quality evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers of each of the 102 languages, with an imposed balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill missing sentence gaps (the ~21.5% missing sentences) in future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker sex (a balance of at least 30/70% sex ratio was imposed when possible) and native language.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, building speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Performance gaps exist across geographical groups; Western European languages have significantly lower CER and higher retrieval scores, partly due to larger amounts of pretraining data, compared to Sub-Saharan African, South Asian, and CJK language groups.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: In the initial release, approximately 21.5% of the sentences are missing due to quality filtering. Multimodal pre-training lags behind on unseen languages and geographical groups known for mixing textual systems or having high homophones (e.g., CJK). Tokenization mismatches can lead to degraded cross-modal retrieval performance in certain languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval, Few-shot learning evaluation of universal representations of speech.
